observations: body L2: the dash after «a)» measures 10.0 pt, that of «104–106» 5.4 pt.
body L4: a heavy bracket opens the addition, which ends on p. 279.
body L12-L13, L25, L40, L43: «Al–Battānī», divided between L12 and L13, and «al–Battānī» are letter-spaced, with long dashes (5.3 and 4.6 pt; 5.3, 5.5 and 5.0 pt).

body L14-L33: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the ecliptic AB, drawn straight through the printed line (which bows by about 0.5 pt between its ends) and broken inside the small ring at S′, as printed; the solid lines L′L², L′λ′, L²λ² and λ′λ² between their meetings; the dotted lines Z′L′, Z²L², L′S′, L²Σ, λ′σ′ and λ²σ² dash by dash, with the dashes that print joined to a line, and the last dash of L′S′ inside the ring at S′; the small rings at λ′, λ², S′ and S²; the bold italic letters, with their primes and superscripts placed as printed; «ecliptica» in italic along AB, with the feathered arrow under it. On the figure L′S′ and λ′σ′ stand at 89.9° and 90.0° to AB and Z′L′λ′ is straight within 0.6°, as L19-L24 require; L²Σ and λ²σ² stand at 89.6° and 88.8° to AB and Z²L²λ² is straight within 0.8°. The arrow points toward B, the direction of increasing longitude, so that σ′ lies behind S′ (L33-L34). The points marked with a 2, and Σ, belong to the second approximation, on p. 278.

body L15, L19-L20, L33: the t of «consistunt» and the e of «tempore» (L15) print with faint bars, like l and c; the L of «Lunae» (L19) prints without its foot, with a speck beside the stem, like «I,unae»; two specks stand before «ad» (L20), one at the height of the capitals and one below the line, like the ends of a bracket, which the sense excludes; the foot of the last t of «scilicet» (L33) prints apart from its stem, like a comma.

body L40-L41: al-Battānī divides the first parallax by the hourly motion of the Moon («per motum horarium inaequalem Lunae», translation, p. 104, l. 21–22; p. 110, l. 11–12), and only the second by the relative motion (p. 104, l. 29–30; p. 110, l. 15–16); adding the minutes of the first parallax to the place of the Moon (p. 104, l. 24–27) then puts the Moon where it is at ϑ + ε′. Dividing S′σ′ by the relative motion, as here and in Schiaparelli's summary on p. 279, is not al-Battānī's rule; ε′ gives only the first approximation, which the second corrects.
